label: First copy step (re-input of first original token) in long sequences, favoring certain first tokens
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase. 91% of activation mass is at recall_idx == 1, the step right after <DEL>, where the input is the first original token fed back and the model outputs original token 1. A small extra slice sits at recall_idx 2, plus a weak tail on the last copy steps of L=9 sequences. Length strongly gates it: L=9 holds 80% of the mass and L=8 holds 19%. It is essentially silent for L<=6, and also on the original phase and the delimiter step. Magnitude depends in a graded way on the identity of the first token (the current input): j, v, r and g are strongest, then o, b, i, w, z, a, k, n; all of the top-activating examples start with j, v or g. (recall_idx==1)&(L>=8) alone gives mass recall 0.90 but precision only 0.32 on dev. Adding the first-token set raises dev F1 to 0.59 (P 0.59, R 0.60, mass 0.75). Because the token dependence is graded rather than a clean set, precision and recall stay incomplete.
